items.title: Al Tinney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002
items.q: his playing foreshadowed that of Bud Powell, Al Haig and Duke Jordan

ctx.x: Pianist Al Tinney was born in Ansonia, Connecticut on May 28, 1921 and died in Buffalo, New York on December 11, 2002. He appeared in the original production of Porgy & Bess as a child performer and later led the house band at Monroe’s Uptown House in New York City. Al took part in the musical experiments that gave birth to bebop and his playing foreshadowed that of Bud Powell, Al Haig and Duke Jordan. He was a well known musical figure in Buffalo and taught and performed at SUNY Buffalo.
Al was interviewed in Buffalo, NY on October 14, 2002 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
